content:
library(shiny)


svg_src <- '
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink" viewBox="-3.217 -127.078 1035.9249329758713 611.7962466487936" width="1035.925" height="611.796">
  <metadata>
    <svglab:export xmlns:svglab="https://svglab.app/ns/" id="7c9b6cf77bbf4603" exportedAt="2026-09-09T18:07:21.459Z" release="0.1.0"/>
  </metadata>
  <rect x="-3.217" y="-127.078" width="1035.9249329758713" height="611.7962466487936" fill="#f7f3ec"/>
  <ellipse id="c2" cx="526.0053619302948" cy="-2.1447721179624324" rx="94.90616621983915" ry="73.19034852546916" stroke="#1d1d1d" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" fill="blue"/>
  <ellipse cx="630.5630026809652" cy="63.00268096514748" rx="133.51206434316353" ry="99.73190348525469" stroke="#1d1d1d" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" fill="none"/>
  <ellipse  cx="740.4628969181218" cy="184.27202505773363" rx="111.67080699510542" ry="114.4846441748733" stroke="#1d1d1d" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" fill="none"/>
  <ellipse cx="455.2278820375335" cy="235.12064343163541" rx="117.42627345844505" ry="88.47184986595175" stroke="#1d1d1d" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" fill="none"/>
  <ellipse cx="405.4504759328055" cy="73.42181403126921" rx="47.519492338342744" ry="18.172165742043372" stroke="#1d1d1d" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" fill="none"/>
  <ellipse cx="170.22898885800709" cy="117.03501181217328" rx="16.63182231841994" ry="123.57072704589493" stroke="#1d1d1d" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" fill="none"/>
  <ellipse cx="471.9777652064863" cy="362.359249329759" rx="161.56627395036523" ry="1.817216574204328" stroke="#1d1d1d" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" fill="none"/>
  <ellipse cx="488.6095875249057" cy="262.4123377485199" rx="11.879873084585686" ry="43.613197780904066" stroke="#1d1d1d" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" fill="none"/>
</svg>
'

myscript <- '
<script>
  circle = document.getElementById("c2");
  circle.addEventListener("click", () => {
    alert("The shape was clicked!");
    Shiny.setInputValue("selected_shape", "dummy");
    Shiny.setInputValue("selected_shape", "router2");
    console.log(circle)
    circle.rx.baseVal.value = 300
  });
</script>
'
mystyle <- '
  <style>
    #circle:hover {
      fill: pink;
      transform: scale(1.1);
    }
  </style>
'
# Define UI for app that draws a histogram ----
ui <- fluidPage(

  # App title ----
  titlePanel("Click on the small diamond"),
  
  HTML(svg_src),
  
  HTML(myscript),
  HTML(mystyle),
  
  actionButton("goButton", "Go!", class = "btn-success"),
  
  # Sidebar layout with input and output definitions ----

    # Sidebar panel for inputs ----

)

# Define server logic required to draw a histogram ----
server <- function(input, output, session) {

  # Histogram of the Old Faithful Geyser Data ----
  # with requested number of bins
  # This expression that generates a histogram is wrapped in a call
  # to renderPlot to indicate that:
  #
  # 1. It is "reactive" and therefore should be automatically
  #    re-executed when inputs (input$bins) change
  # 2. Its output type is a plot
  
  observeEvent(input$selected_shape, {
    print(input$selected_shape)
  })
  
  output$distPlot <- renderPlot({

    x    <- faithful$waiting
    bins <- seq(min(x), max(x), length.out = input$bins + 1)

    hist(x, breaks = bins, col = "#75AADB", border = "white",
         xlab = "Waiting time to next eruption (in mins)",
         main = "Histogram of waiting times")

    })
  
  observeEvent(input$goButton, {
    print(content(res1))
    updateTextAreaInput(session, "caption", value = res1$status_code)
  })

}

# Create Shiny app ----
shinyApp(ui = ui, server = server)

name: Readme.md
content:
This small Shiny application demonstrates Shiny's automatic UI updates. 

Move the *Number of bins* slider and notice how the `renderPlot` expression is automatically re-evaluated when its dependant, `input$bins`, changes, causing a histogram with a new number of bins to be rendered.
